record.original_question: For arrangements (L, P) of construction lines and registration marks in the Euclidean plane with k >= 3 registration marks, can any valid arrangement determine more than k + 1 construction lines while still obeying the rules that every point of P is an intersection of at least two lines in L and every two nonparallel lines in L intersect in a unique point of P? Equivalently, is it true that every such arrangement has at most k + 1 construction lines?

evidence.quote: It is reasonable to ask then, are there any arrangements containing shapes with k registration marks such that they determine greater than k + 1 construction lines?
We conjecture that such arrangements do not exist: Conjecture 1. At most k + 1 construction lines are determined by k >= 3 registration marks in the plane.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. Call a finite pair $(L,P)$, where $L$ is a finite set of distinct lines (called construction lines) and $P$ is a finite set of distinct points (called registration marks), a valid arrangement if:

(i) every point of $P$ lies on at least two lines of $L$ (i.e., each registration mark is an intersection of at least two construction lines), and

(ii) for any two non-parallel lines $\ell_1,\ell_2 \in L$, their unique intersection point belongs to $P$.

Let $k = |P| \geq 3$. Prove or disprove the following statement: every valid arrangement $(L,P)$ satisfies $|L| \leq k+1$. Equivalently, show that no valid arrangement with $k \geq 3$ registration marks can determine more than $k+1$ construction lines.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for this conjecture about bounding the number of construction lines by k+1 in terms of the number of registration marks did not return any direct resolution or follow-up work. While related results in incidence geometry (Sylvester–Gallai, Dirac–Motzkin, supersolvable line arrangements) exist, none specifically resolve this exact upper-bound conjecture, so the current status is unclear from the available evidence.

status_evidence.claim: The general line-arrangement literature does not appear to contain a resolution of this specific conjecture.

status_evidence.snippet: Classical incidence-geometry result related to lines and their intersection points.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related incidence-geometry results exist but do not directly settle the stated upper bound.
